extra.reason: Timer-driven control loop implemented, validated on hardware, and documented. 78 ns jitter and 0 missed deadlines at the plan's 50 ms tick; rate ceiling ~16-20 kHz measured; overload shown to degrade timing but not correctness. Docs updated in firmware/ctrl/README.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md and TODO.md.

Probe runs on the H743 with an RTT console. DTCM placement, 240 MHz cycle counter and fpu_dp=1 confirmed on hardware; cache A/B run and compared against the F767 (not free here, ~2%, unlike the F767's bit-identical result). Results and the three RTT traps recorded in firmware/BRINGUP.md.

firmware/ctrl runs on the H743 with a plant-only plan and reproduces the backend digest bit-for-bit (0x6a01864d4f8e0c87). Proves a plant needs no new firmware, only a different .dcp, and gives a fourth architecture for the determinism claim. New fixture 05-plant-only is regression-protected in both test suites.

Cause found: the H743's D-cache. Measured all four board/cache combinations on the same plan - F767 caches are free to the cycle, H743 caches are 3.6x throughput and 24x jitter, and with caches off the two boards are nearly identical. The cpu_awake outlier is cache-correlated and disappears with them off. Documented, with the consequence that the plant board should likely run caches off for E3.
